title: Alberta Votes on a Big Question About Canada
summary:
Alberta is a province in western Canada. On Monday, people there are voting. They are not choosing right now whether to leave Canada. They are choosing whether to hold a special vote about leaving later. That kind of vote is called a referendum.

Alberta's leader, Danielle Smith, called the vote after a group gathered about 300,000 names on a petition. Another petition against leaving got more than 400,000 names. About five million people live in Alberta.

Some people want Alberta to leave. They say Canada's rules about the environment have hurt Alberta's oil-rich economy. Others, including Prime Minister Mark Carney, want Alberta to stay. Polls suggest most people there want to stay.

A court said the petition to leave did not ask First Nations, Indigenous groups whose land would be affected. Smith does not want Alberta to leave, but she says people should have their say.

If voters say yes, a final vote could happen as soon as 2027.
why_it_matters: It shows how people in a democracy can vote on big questions about their own future.
